standard.title: Draw conclusions based on analysis
standard.description: draw conclusions based on analysis of information
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y2 (AC9HS2S05): Students drew evidence-based conclusions about significance, technology change and place connections.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students draw conclusions about community change, place features and people's connections with places, based on analysis of information.

nodes.label: Drawing evidence-based conclusions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can draw conclusions about how their place and community have changed, the preservation of environmental features, and how people are connected to places, based on analysed data and information.
nodes.minimum_width: Draw at least one conclusion about community change, an environmental feature or a place connection, supported by at least two pieces of analysed evidence.
nodes.typical_width: Reach conclusions about: how place and community have changed based on settlement patterns, local species changes, historic events or cultural celebrations; preservation of unique natural features; similarities and differences of places in Australia and neighbouring countries.
wider: Draw conclusions that connect community change to broader patterns (e.g. immigration, environmental policy) beyond the local area
Compare conclusions drawn from different source types on the same topic and discuss which are strongest

response_modes.reason: Year 3 conclusions must be grounded in analysis, not just impression — use structured evidence-to-conclusion templates to make the reasoning visible.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Drawing conclusions across multiple domains (community change, environment, place connections) at Year 3 builds transferable analytical reasoning that underpins all future HASS inquiry.
success_criteria: States at least one conclusion supported by at least two pieces of evidence
Conclusion responds to an inquiry question rather than restating a fact
